page: Microsoft Azure D48plds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine instance belonging to the DPLDSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at a sustained frequency of 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core allocation. It is equipped with 1843 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks highlight a strong multi-core capability, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and software compilation via Clang scoring in the top 25 percent tier. Conversely, single-core performance is more modest, with Geekbench single-core and bzip3 single-threaded decompression scoring in the lower 25 percent tier. Memory bandwidth is stable, registering 176.14 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 76.83 GB/sec for large block write operations. Large-scale LLM inference is limited, with prompt processing for a 70B model falling into the bottom 10 percent tier, though text generation for the same model remains average.

This instance offers a cost-efficient profile for multi-threaded, compute-intensive workloads that do not require high memory-to-core ratios. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it suitable for scale-out applications, software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, and web serving, where physical core density and local storage capacity are prioritized over massive memory footprints.
